name: Youth Counselor

sections.daily_work: Support young people through emotional, behavioral, and academic challenges. Provide guidance, mentorship, and crisis intervention in schools, community programs, or residential settings.
sections.learning: Counseling techniques, child and adolescent psychology, crisis intervention, conflict resolution, understanding of youth development and family dynamics.
sections.pay: Varies by setting and credentials. Entry-level often starts around $30,000-$45,000 USD. Licensed counselors may earn more. Always verify current data for your region.
sections.entry_routes: Degree in psychology, counseling, or social work, internships in youth programs, mentoring or tutoring experience, certification in youth counseling.

try_in_real_life: Volunteer as a mentor or tutor for younger students
Learn about common challenges facing youth in your community
Practice conflict resolution and active listening skills
Research youth counseling programs and certification requirements
sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook Handbook (bls.gov/ooh)
